question.problem:
Calculate the number of terms in the following arithmetic series.

$$
5+15+25+…=180
$$
question.worked_solution:
To solve this problem, we use the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series:

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d)\,\,
$$

We have been given the sum ${S}_{N}=180$, and the first term ${a}_{1}=5.$ Our goal is to find $N,$ the number of terms.

The common difference $d$ can be found, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{2}-{a}_{1} \\  & =15-5 \\  & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these values into the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d) \\ 180 & =\frac{N}{2}(2\cdot 5+(N-1)\cdot 10) \\ 180 & =\frac{N}{2}(10+10N-10) \\ 180 & =\frac{N}{2}(10N) \\ 180 & =5{N}^{2} \\ 36 & ={N}^{2} \\ N & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we take the positive square root because $N$can't be negative. Therefore, our series has $N=6$ terms.
